tasks.short: Develop and teach online history courses

steps.what: Develop course outcomes, select historical sources, and specify online learning activities
Write online course explanations and activity instructions from the course brief

loop.purpose: Draft explanations and instructions within the teacher's course design
loop.input: course brief and selected source extracts
loop.check: Teacher checks historical interpretation, factual claims, reading level and activity alignment against the sources
loop.stop: One revision; unresolved historical claims or unsuitable activities are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Native course templates organize modules but cannot write contextual historical explanations

steps.what: Check, publish, maintain, and teach the online courses

tasks.design: Use native {LMS} module templates first, with a bounded drafting loop in {DOCS} for source-grounded explanations. The teacher checks the complete course version, publishes it and continues teaching and maintenance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drafting explanatory text required repeated composition even when the teacher had already selected sources and outcomes.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded writing assistant can turn a teacher-authored brief into an editable draft.
tasks.still_hard: Historical ambiguity, accessibility and productive online discussion need teacher judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher chooses interpretations, challenges students and responds to misunderstanding.
tasks.altitude: A small amount of composition time becomes available for improving learning activities; teaching authority is unchanged.

reach.task: Review alignment of online activities with learning outcomes

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting of course explanations is a plausible bounded assistance pattern; this design and its savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers teacher course design, composition, publication, maintenance and teaching; assessment and student enrolment are outside this task.

The history teacher produces the course brief in s1: outcomes, audience, module order, source extracts with page references, activity purpose and accessibility requirements. Capture and source selection time remain fully counted; incomplete briefs return to manual composition.
Test native LMS templates and content reuse before custom code; existing runtime earns no saving.
Teaching, final checks, publishing and maintenance in s3 retain their whole baseline. No student personal data enter the drafting loop.
unknowns: Existing course templates and reuse rate
Source licensing and approved drafting environment
research_questions: Does drafting save composition time after checking historical claims and activity instructions?

already_counted.description: Review and correction of proposed explanations

incremental.description: Maintain source handling and draft checks
Learning platform support for templates and access

approvals.approved_version: Exact course content, activities, source references and audience version checked in s3; any edit requires another check before publication

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R91.25 gives gross8.75 minus4 upkeep =4.75 net. Range0-2 assumes limited reusable explanatory passages and substantial historical verification; teaching and maintenance do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in campus and community events

steps.what: Participate in campus and community events through discussion and personal engagement

tasks.design: Participation remains personal. Event notices in {CALENDAR} can support attendance without replacing the teacher's engagement.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work consists of being present and responding to people.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar tools already support logistics; they do not perform participation.
tasks.still_hard: Trust and spontaneous discussion depend on the individual teacher.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher represents their discipline and forms relationships.
tasks.altitude: Participation and decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Engage public audiences at community events

evidence.claim: In-person participation cannot be replaced by calendar automation while preserving personal engagement.

assumptions: Boundary is participation itself; event production and institutional scheduling belong to event organizers and earn no saving here.
No automated step consumes structured data; the teacher interprets event context directly.
Consider native calendar functions for existing logistics without inventing a clerical baseline.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool, model or workflow is introduced.
unknowns: Mix of public and campus events
research_questions: Which parts of participation do audiences value as personal engagement?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 minus0 upkeep gives net0. Both small campus gatherings and public events retain personal participation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Act as advisers to student organizations through discussion of plans and concerns

tasks.design: Keep advising as a conversation. Approved guidance in {DOCS} remains a reference for the teacher and students.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task involves judgement about student plans and relationships.
tasks.enabler_now: A searchable guidance library may help locate policies but does not replace advising.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting interests and sensitive concerns require contextual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The adviser supports student autonomy and recognizes when specialist help is needed.
tasks.altitude: Advising responsibilities and time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Facilitation without taking over student decisions

evidence.claim: Student organization advising is contextual dialogue; no measured automation benefit is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is advising; student administration and organization management stay with their existing owners and are not transferred to the teacher.
Students describe plans and concerns during the conversation; no free structured suitability or risk flag is assumed.
Use existing document search before considering a new assistant; no new system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because the process remains unchanged.
unknowns: Nature of organizations and adviser responsibilities
research_questions: Do advisers have repeated policy lookup work distinct from their conversations?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 and upkeep0 net0. Routine planning advice and difficult interpersonal cases both retain the human conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose sources and plan community courses for the audience
Prepare explanatory handouts for community courses and local groups

loop.purpose: Draft plain explanations from selected historical material
loop.input: community teaching brief with source extracts
loop.check: Teacher checks chronology, interpretation, source fidelity and suitability for the local audience
loop.stop: One revision; disputed or unsupported wording is rewritten manually
loop.why_not_simpler: A document template handles layout but cannot adapt historical explanations to the audience

steps.what: Check handouts, teach community courses, and speak with local groups

tasks.design: Use a native {DOCS} handout template and a bounded source-grounded drafting loop. The teacher checks handouts before sharing and delivers the community teaching personally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Adapting source material into short public explanations took composition time.
tasks.enabler_now: Writing assistance can propose editable audience-specific wording from selected extracts.
tasks.still_hard: Local sensitivities and live questions require knowledge and judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher connects historical interpretation to the audience's questions.
tasks.altitude: A small preparation saving leaves delivery responsibilities unchanged.

reach.task: Develop accessible historical interpretation for public audiences

evidence.claim: Drafting public-facing explanations from teacher-selected sources is plausible assistance; benefits are task-specific estimates.

assumptions: Boundary includes this event's preparation and delivery; room booking, promotion and student grading are outside it.

The history teacher produces audience description, duration, topic, source extracts with page references and learning purpose in s1. All capture time is counted there; absent source context requires manual writing.
Test native templates and existing handout reuse before adding the drafting loop.
If an online course supplies the same handout, assign its preparation once in the roll-up rather than adding both tasks.
research_questions: Does checked drafting reduce handout preparation for unfamiliar community audiences?

already_counted.description: Review and correction of handout wording

incremental.description: Maintain drafting instructions and source checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact checked handout text, images and source references shared in s3; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R95.5 gross4.5 minus2 upkeep gives net2.5. Range0-1 assumes short handouts, substantial source checking and unchanged live teaching.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Small reductions in explanatory drafting leave historical judgement, teaching and community relationships with the teacher.
reach: Coordinate accessible learning activities with instructional coordinators
Learn public interpretation approaches from curators
role.ambitious_version: A history teacher with more time to refine activities while preserving direct engagement with students and public audiences.
